selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Per-neighbor/per-neighbor-group rewrite of VPNv4 and VPNv6 NEXT_HOP to the local interface address when reflecting VPN address-family routes; distinct from IPv4/IPv6 unicast next-hop-self.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: VPNv4/VPNv6 UPDATE received by RR -> route reflection decision -> AF-specific NEXT_HOP rewrite -> UPDATE to RR client -> client resolves new transport next hop and installs VPN route.
selected_topics.failure_class: Reflected VPN route retains an unreachable originating PE next hop; VPNv4/v6 forwarding fails despite route presence.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: BGP neighbor session is Established and VPN route is received, but routing-table gateway remains the remote PE address or recursive resolution fails; compare advertised/received route attributes before and after AF-specific setting.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Upgrade to FortiOS 8.0.0 or later; enable next-hop-self-rr-vpnv4 and/or next-hop-self-rr-vpnv6 at neighbor or neighbor-group scope; verify the RR local interface is reachable in the transport table.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: A VPNv6 route is reflected but the client cannot resolve the originating PE next hop; select the address-family-specific RR rewrite rather than changing RT import or global IPv4 next-hop behavior.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Three-node PE-A -> RR -> PE-B topology with VPNv4/VPNv6 control-plane UPDATE and rewritten RR next-hop highlighted; transport reachability shown separately.
selected_topics.semantic_uniqueness: No materially equivalent VPNv4/VPNv6 RR next-hop rewrite lesson in the 402-record rolling inventory; prior BGP route-map, conditional-advertisement, TCP-AO and ADVPN topics use different mechanisms.
selected_topics.scenario_age_note: Community scenario is approximately eight months old; used as a mechanism-specific failure example, not represented as a newly published 30-day item.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: FortiSASE multi-instance central management across FortiCloud organization hierarchy
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager 8.0 Device Manager treats multiple FortiSASE instances as managed devices; eligibility is constrained by FortiCare account or parent/child OU relationship, and each instance is placed in an ADOM.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiSASE central-management enablement -> optional non-expiring FortiManager Key generation -> FortiManager device registration -> ADOM association -> one-way configuration/object synchronization from FortiManager to FortiSASE.
selected_topics.failure_class: Tenant cannot be onboarded or central-management sync fails because account/OU ancestry, key, ADOM mode, unique device name, or synchronization direction is misunderstood.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Device-add failure for invalid OU/account relationship, missing/revoked key, duplicate name, Backup/Global/7.0 ADOM, or an object deleted on FortiManager that conflicts with one-way synchronization.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Validate FortiCloud Organization ancestry and FortiCare account, generate and copy the tenant FortiManager Key when required, use a supported non-Backup ADOM, assign a unique instance name, and treat FortiManager as the configuration source of truth.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: An MSSP manages several SASE instances from one FMG; choose the required OU/key and ADOM relationship and preserve one-way source-of-truth semantics.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: MSSP root FortiCare/OU with child OUs, one FortiManager, separate FortiSASE instances mapped one-per-ADOM; one-way arrows for configuration sync and separate ZTNA telemetry channel.
selected_topics.semantic_uniqueness: No matching FortiManager-to-FortiSASE multi-instance/OU/key workflow in the rolling inventory; previous FMG topics covered ADOM object mapping, FortiGuard package control, workflow locking and templates.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: SAML administrator SSO signature and digest algorithm migration to SHA-256/SHA-512
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer IdP and SP SAML settings independently select RSA-SHA256 or RSA-SHA512 signature algorithm and SHA256 or SHA512 digest; SHA-1 support is removed; asymmetric trust allows IdP and SP to use different supported choices.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Browser AuthnRequest -> IdP authentication -> signed SAML Response/Assertion -> SP signature and digest validation -> admin identity/profile/ADOM mapping -> session creation.
selected_topics.failure_class: SAML login rejection caused by algorithm incompatibility, invalid signature/certificate, missing local/wildcard admin, or RelayState/ACS URL mismatch.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: SAML tracer shows AuthnRequest, Response, assertion signature/digest and destination/ACS; `get system saml` exposes settings; `diagnose system admin-session list` confirms the resulting SSO profile and ADOM.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Replace SHA-1 with supported RSA-SHA256/RSA-SHA512 and SHA256/SHA512, align IdP/SP certificates and signing requirements, verify ACS/RelayState, and ensure admin/profile/ADOM mapping exists on the SP.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: An IdP uses RSA-SHA256 while the FortiAnalyzer SP uses SHA-512; determine whether different supported algorithms are allowed and separate signature/digest faults from RelayState faults.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Browser between IdP and FortiAnalyzer SP; AuthnRequest and signed Response arrows; certificates and algorithm/digest validation shown at both endpoints; admin profile/ADOM mapping after validation.
selected_topics.semantic_uniqueness: No FortiAnalyzer SAML signature/digest algorithm negotiation lesson in the 402-record inventory; prior SAML topics covered proxying and identity routing on other products.
selected_topics.scenario_age_note: Community SAML login article is older and focuses on RelayState/ACS; it is used only as an adjacent diagnostic boundary, not as a recent signature-algorithm scenario.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Per-neighbor BGP local-AS identity for multi-AS transition and AS-path control
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitchOS 8.0 allows a BGP speaker with mandatory global `set as` to present a neighbor-specific `local-as`, with local-as-no-prepend and local-as-replace controls for outbound AS_PATH identity.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Global BGP process starts with real ASN -> per-neighbor local-AS selected for OPEN/update behavior -> outbound AS_PATH is constructed according to prepend/replace controls -> peer applies loop detection and route policy.
selected_topics.failure_class: Peering or route advertisement fails during ASN migration because remote-as, local-as, and AS_PATH presentation are inconsistent or the global AS is omitted.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: BGP session state and received/advertised route AS_PATH differ from expected; neighbor details show peer relationship while route table may remain empty due to loop detection or eBGP policy.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Keep global ASN and router ID configured; set local-as only on the affected neighbor; use no-prepend/replace only for the intended path semantics; confirm platform/model support and inspect the peer's received AS_PATH.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: A switch must peer with a partner expecting a temporary ASN while retaining its internal global ASN; choose neighbor-scoped local-AS and validate AS_PATH instead of changing the whole BGP process.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiSwitch with global ASN and one neighbor-specific local-AS eBGP adjacency to a peer; global identity and per-neighbor advertised identity shown as separate labels.
selected_topics.semantic_uniqueness: No FortiSwitch neighbor-local-AS/multi-AS lesson in the rolling inventory; prior switch topics covered BGP EVPN multihoming and L2/port controls, not ASN presentation.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Wi-Fi 7 Multi-Link Operation on FortiAP K-series, including local standalone operation
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: 802.11be MLO forms one logical multi-link device association across supported 2.4/5/6-GHz radios; FortiAP-K support begins at FAP 7.6.3, while local standalone MLO requires FAP 7.6.5 and local bridge/authentication controls.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client discovers MLO-capable SSID -> WPA3/OWE security and H2E requirements satisfied -> multi-link association establishes link IDs across eligible radios -> WTP profile advertises VAP on radios -> AP/controller or standalone AP handles authentication and traffic.
selected_topics.failure_class: MLO SSID is configured but client falls back to a single link or cannot join because model/radio/firmware/security/profile prerequisites are not met.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: `diagnose wpa wpad mld` reports MLD and `num_links`/link IDs; AP `vcfg | grep mlo` confirms VAP flag; client association and radio profile show actual link use.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Check exact FortiAP-K model/radio support and firmware, use WPA3-SAE with H2E-only, WPA3 Enterprise Only or OWE, enable `mlo`, attach VAP to the required radio profiles, and add local-standalone/local-bridging/local-authentication only for standalone bridge mode.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: A K-series AP advertises an MLO SSID but a client uses one link; identify the model/radio/firmware/security prerequisite and the correct MLD evidence.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: One MLD client associated to a FortiAP-K with parallel 2.4/5/6-GHz link paths, one logical SSID/VAP, and a controller-vs-local-standalone authentication boundary.
selected_topics.semantic_uniqueness: No Wi-Fi 7 MLO multi-link association or standalone operation lesson in the 402-record inventory; previous wireless lessons addressed MPSK/VLAN, DFS, CCA, DHCP option and roaming.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Certificate-backed FortiNAC server trust plus allowed-serial-number admission control
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC 9.4.3+ inter-server communication requires certificate-bearing license keys and an explicit `security.allowedserialnumbers` allowlist; Manager/managed-server/HA roles have asymmetric allowlist membership.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Server startup/peer connection -> local certificate presence check -> peer serial-number allowlist check -> mutually authorized Manager/managed-server or HA communication -> database/config replication for secondary.
selected_topics.failure_class: Manager cannot add or synchronize a managed FortiNAC-OS server, or HA peer emits unauthorized-connection events after upgrade.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: System Summary shows Certificates=Yes; `licensetool` lists certificate serials; `globaloptiontool -name security.allowedserialnumbers` returns the allowlist; community event identifies remote IP and serial.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Install valid certificate-bearing license keys or exchange self-signed certificates on older appliances; populate role-correct serial lists; apply on HA primary where replication copies configuration; verify the stored list even if the CLI prints the documented unknown-option warning.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: A managed server disappears after an upgrade even though IP reachability is good; identify certificate presence and role-correct allowed serial list rather than changing RADIUS or switch discovery.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC Manager, managed servers, and HA primary/secondary with certificate trust in both directions and asymmetric allowed-serial lists; replication arrow from primary to secondary.
selected_topics.semantic_uniqueness: No FortiNAC server-to-server certificate/serial allowlist admission-control lesson in the 402-record inventory; previous NAC topics covered endpoint profiling, RADIUS, LDAP, agents and MDM.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: FortiNAC-F managed VDOM multi-tenancy with shared FortiLink infrastructure and tenant VLAN enforcement
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F identifies the tenant VDOM associated with a managed FortiSwitch port and applies the tenant's logical-network VLAN; FortiGate root/MGMT VDOM owns shared FortiLink infrastructure while ports and VLANs are exported into tenant VDOMs.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiGate root manages switch/AP -> physical switch port exported to tenant VDOM -> tenant VLAN/VDOM-link routing and policy established -> FortiNAC discovers root and tenant virtual devices -> host classification selects registration/remediation/production VLAN within tenant VDOM.
selected_topics.failure_class: Endpoint is placed in the wrong tenant VLAN or loses NAC/DHCP/external connectivity because port export, tenant VLAN, VDOM link, routing, policy, or virtual-device mapping is incomplete.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: FortiNAC Virtualized Devices lists root and tenant VDOMs; exported port is grayed in root and visible in tenant; registration/production VLANs resolve to tenant VLAN IDs; DHCP and routing tests follow the VDOM link.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Use FortiLink-managed FortiSwitch; create tenant VDOM and VDOM link; export the port; create tenant VLANs and default virtual-switch VLAN; add policies/routes in both VDOMs; map FortiNAC logical networks to tenant VLANs and define isolation DHCP scopes.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: A shared switch port is visible in the tenant but a quarantined host receives a root-VLAN address; trace port export, VDOM link, tenant VLAN mapping and DHCP scope.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Root/MGMT VDOM managing one FortiSwitch and FortiAP, exported access port into tenant traffic VDOM, VDOM link to root, FortiNAC discovery and separate registration/remediation/production VLANs.
selected_topics.semantic_uniqueness: No FortiNAC-F FortiGate VDOM multi-tenant port-export/host-placement workflow in the 402-record inventory; previous NAC-F lessons covered endpoint identity, MDM and captive portal flows.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: RADIUS client groups and authentication-profile separation in policy selection
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.2 groups RADIUS client definitions and separates authentication profiles from RADIUS policies; a policy can reference clients or groups, up to two RADIUS attribute criteria, credential type and an authentication profile.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Access-Request source IP -> most-specific client definition -> candidate policy membership -> optional attribute match -> credential-type match -> first/topmost matching policy -> authentication profile and identity/factor evaluation -> Access-Accept/Reject.
selected_topics.failure_class: Valid RADIUS client receives Access-Reject or wrong authentication flow because client group membership, policy ordering, source-range overlap, attribute criteria, or profile binding is incorrect.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: RADIUS request source IP and attributes identify candidate client; policy order and client-group membership explain selected rule; RADIUS logs show daemon restart after config change and resulting accept/reject.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Create precise client address objects, group only intended clients, bind groups to ordered policies, set the correct credential type/profile, constrain attribute criteria, and verify the narrowest overlapping client range wins.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: Two overlapping client subnets match one request but different authentication profiles are intended; choose the most-specific client match and topmost eligible policy, not the user-group membership.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Multiple AP/switch/NAS RADIUS clients feeding client groups, ordered policy matcher (source/client, attributes, credential type), authentication profile and identity source, then Access-Accept/Reject.
selected_topics.semantic_uniqueness: No FortiAuthenticator RADIUS client-group plus authentication-profile policy-selection workflow in the 402-record inventory; prior FAC lessons covered RADSec accounting, LDAP, FSSO, SAML and OTP.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Regex-based launcher process matching for multi-process and Java applications
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM 1.9 launcher can identify the target application by initial process, GUI window-title regex, or command-line regex rather than relying only on executable name; custom matchers force multi-process monitoring and full-screen recording.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User launches privileged app through launcher -> process tree is monitored -> matcher evaluates window title or command line -> matching process is treated as target -> full-screen session recording preserves audit context.
selected_topics.failure_class: Privileged application is launched but not recognized or recording misses the target window because Java/child processes or window renaming break executable-only matching.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Launcher definition shows matcher type/pattern; multiprocess and fullscreen-record are enabled; session recording captures the entire desktop and target window; process tree includes the child Java/IDE process.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Use a narrow anchored regex against stable window-title or command-line content, enable multi-process mode and full-screen recording, then test the actual launch path and confirm the resulting session recording.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: An IDE spawns java.exe with variable child processes and renamed windows; choose command-line/window-title matching and preserve the forced process-tree/full-screen audit controls.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM session broker -> launcher -> parent process and child process tree -> regex matcher -> monitored full-screen recording stream.
selected_topics.semantic_uniqueness: No FortiPAM process matcher or process-tree selection lesson in the 402-record inventory; prior PAM lessons covered launcher privilege, API tokens, session approval, secret rotation and recording.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Python-based custom external threat-feed ingestion and Full versus Incremental update semantics
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSIEM custom feed integration invokes a Python plugin from the Supervisor-side threatfeedIntegrations directory, passes feed URL/credentials/arguments, writes normalized CSV for AppServer parsing, and supports Full replacement or Incremental addition.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Scheduled feed task -> plugin invocation with URL/credentials -> HTTPS/TLS retrieval and parsing -> normalized CSV output -> AppServer ingestion -> IOC group update -> scheduled next run.
selected_topics.failure_class: Feed appears configured but IOC group is stale/empty because plugin path, script interface, TLS verification, authentication, parser format, or Full/Incremental semantics are wrong.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Threat-feed group and schedule exist; plugin is selected as Python; SSL Verify state and URL/credentials are correct; CSV output is produced and new IOC rows appear after the scheduled update.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Install the script under `/opt/phoenix/data-definition/threatfeedIntegrations/`, use the documented plugin interface, enable SSL verification, validate credentials/URL and CSV normalization, and choose Full only when replacement is intended.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: A feed refresh removes valid existing IOCs after a successful fetch; distinguish Full replacement from Incremental append and select the correct update semantics.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: External STIX/TAXII/API feed -> FortiSIEM Supervisor Python plugin -> normalized CSV handoff -> AppServer parser -> Malware IP/URL/Domain/Hash group and schedule.
selected_topics.semantic_uniqueness: No FortiSIEM Python custom-feed execution or Full/Incremental ingestion workflow in the 402-record inventory; previous SIEM topics covered analytics, watchlists, correlation, ML and data ingestion.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Event-triggered vulnerability scanning on endpoint software changes
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSASE endpoint Protection profile can trigger vulnerability scans when new software is installed/detected, existing software is updated, or a potentially unwanted application is detected; this is distinct from scheduled and connection/OS/signature-update triggers.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Endpoint software inventory change detected -> endpoint profile event trigger fires -> FortiClient vulnerability scan runs -> findings are reported to FortiSASE -> optional user popup/remediation/automatic patch behavior follows configured controls.
selected_topics.failure_class: New or updated software remains unassessed because the trigger is disabled, endpoint profile is not assigned, detection does not occur, or scan results are mistaken for automatic patching.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Protection profile shows Event-based scanning and Trigger vulnerability scan on software change; endpoint inventory records the changed app/PUA; scan result timestamp follows the change event; patch status is separate.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Enable the software-change trigger in the assigned endpoint profile, confirm FortiClient/SASE compatibility and endpoint inventory detection, verify a scan event and result, and separately configure patching if automatic remediation is intended.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: A new PUA is installed between weekly scans; choose the software-change event trigger and verify a scan, rather than assuming scheduled scanning or patching ran.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Managed endpoint software inventory event -> FortiClient trigger -> FortiSASE endpoint profile -> vulnerability scan/signature evaluation -> findings and optional patch/remediation branch.
selected_topics.semantic_uniqueness: No FortiSASE software-change/PUA-triggered vulnerability scan lesson in the 402-record inventory; prior SASE lessons covered tunnel autoconnect, bandwidth, ZTNA, browser and posture controls.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: ToS-mask matching for selective SD-WAN packet duplication and de-duplication
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS 8.0 SD-WAN duplication rules can match the 8-bit ToS field using `tos` and `tos-mask`; source/destination, interface, service and zone constraints select which packets are duplicated, with corresponding de-duplication at the receiving side.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Ingress packet classified by duplication rule -> ToS & mask comparison plus address/interface/service criteria -> packet copies sent over eligible zone members -> remote de-duplication rule recognizes matching copies -> one logical packet forwarded.
selected_topics.failure_class: Critical traffic is not duplicated or unrelated traffic is replicated because ToS value/mask, source/destination criteria, zone members, maximum duplication count, or receiver de-duplication rule is mismatched.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Rule configuration shows ToS/mask and packet-duplication mode; packet captures on multiple zone members show copies only for matching DS-field values; receiver-side de-duplication prevents duplicate delivery.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Set a narrow ToS pattern and mask, align source/destination/service criteria on sender and receiver, verify zone membership and duplication maximum, and test both matching and non-matching traffic.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: Only packets marked with a designated ToS value should be duplicated across four zone members; select a masked duplication rule and matching receiver de-duplication rather than FEC or generic load balancing.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Sender FortiGate with four SD-WAN zone members duplicates matching ToS traffic across paths; receiver FortiGate de-duplicates copies before forwarding; non-matching traffic follows a single path.
selected_topics.semantic_uniqueness: No SD-WAN packet-duplication rule or ToS-mask selective replication lesson in the 402-record inventory; prior SD-WAN lessons covered FEC, SLA, quota, traffic steering and per-packet load balancing.
